The wrapper earns a name only as the arbitrary-field counterpart of the kbar one; it adds no mathematics. Docstring already concedes this ("the proof is mathlibs 0BFD plus one instance") -- it is honest, just not new.

(4) THE HEADLINE CLAIM IS DEFENSIBLE BUT MUST BE NARROWED. "The field hypothesis is not among the reasons isAlbanese_pic0Et is open" is supported for the CONSUMER side (the two rigidity inputs the engine consumes are now arbitrary-field). It is NOT supported for the SUPPLY side, and the second clause "its content ... the descent datum ... is" understates the coupling: the only route that PRODUCES hdesc geometrically is exists_unique_descent_of_section / _of_birational (AlbaneseFromData.lean:266,:312), both under `variable {kbar} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]` declared at :253, and neither is transported by these files. Its own engine extend_to_av / exists_unique_hom_restrict_eq_of_dense_open (DenseOpenDescent.lean:132) is likewise under [IsAlgClosed kbar] at :77. So the field hypothesis is still load-bearing exactly where the descent datum is manufactured. Also note the kbar rigidity original needed IsAlgClosed for ONE reason only -- isReduced_tensorObj_self_left, via Scheme.isReduced_of_smooth_of_isAlgClosed (measured: geometricallyIrreducible_tensorObj_self and locallyOfFiniteType_tensorObj_self carry NO IsAlgClosed). Honest phrasing: "the field hypothesis is removable on the two rigidity INPUTS; it remains on the descent-datum SUPPLY route, which these files do not touch."' 2>&1 | tail -5
